extra.message: Authentication failures are handled by flashing 'Incorrect Login' to the user and re-rendering the form; no durable security audit record is produced. Neither this handler nor any shared hook, decorator, or logging configuration in the application records failed logins, successful logins (line 51), logouts, or account creation (lines 62-64), so credential-guessing attacks and account takeover leave no detectable trace for monitoring or incident response.

State-changing POST endpoints (/register/ here, and /login at line 41) accept form submissions with no anti-CSRF token: the application does not initialise Flask-WTF/CSRFProtect, no token is generated or verified server-side, and the corresponding forms in templates/register.html and templates/login.html contain no hidden token field. Session cookies default to SameSite unset, so a malicious site can force a logged-in victim's browser to submit these forms (e.g. registering attacker-controlled accounts or session-fixation style login CSRF).
